prompt: Here's a NestJS controller that streams an LLM completion to the browser over SSE — the client renders tokens as they arrive and has a "Stop / Abort" button that just closes the HTTP connection. QA reports that clicking Abort does nothing server-side: generation still runs to completion, the provider still gets billed for every token, and the logs show a clean `done` frame as if the client never left. Walk through this code and tell me exactly why "the client left" never turns into "stop generating" — trace both lifecycles (the HTTP connection and the token-generation loop) and give me the precise fix, without touching how we call into the provider itself.
